title: Optimizing Distributed ML Communication with Fused Computation-Collective Operations
problem: Collective communication is often the critical bottleneck in distributed ML training across multiple nodes. Without independent computation kernels executing concurrently, communication latency cannot be hidden through overlap.
motivation: Reducing communication overhead is essential to improving scalability and efficiency of distributed machine learning training.
method: Instead of finishing all computations first and then sending results between GPUs, this approach combines these operations into a single program (kernel) that runs on the GPU. Groups of GPU threads can immediately send their results directly to other GPUs while other thread groups continue computing—with the GPU itself managing the sending rather than the CPU (GPU-initiated communication). The team developed three specific combined operations: embedding plus All-to-All communication, GEMV (matrix-vector multiplication) plus AllReduce, and GEMM (matrix-matrix multiplication) plus All-to-All, each optimized for specific AI architectures—DLRM, Transformer, and Mixture-of-Experts. These are exposed as PyTorch operators and integrated into the Triton framework.
key_novelty: Fusing computation with direct GPU-to-GPU communication at the threadblock level (groups of GPU threads), enabling simultaneous data transfer and computation in a single kernel.
contributions: Fused computation-collective operator design that overlaps communication with computation
Three prototype implementations targeting major ML architectures (DLRM, Transformers, MoE)
Integration as PyTorch operators and Triton framework extensions
12-31% execution time reduction across all three fused operators
primary_theme: overlapping communication and computation in distributed ML via fused kernels
